claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is homogeneous and single-phase.
High-temperature pre-annealing of the FeNiCrCoCu coating will refine its near-surface microstructure.
Pre-annealing can produce nanoscale features such as increased twin density in the coating.
Pre-annealing may produce nanoprecipitates or Cu-segregated regions in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The annealing-induced microstructure will impede dislocation motion during high-temperature sliding.
The annealing-induced microstructure will impede grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature sliding.
A refined near-surface microstructure can contribute to improved wear resistance.
Compared with the untreated coating, the pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu coating will have a statistically significant decrease in wear rate.
Compared with the untreated coating, the pre-annealed FeNiCrCoCu coating will undergo less microscopic plastic deformation.
The predicted wear and deformation effects will operate during sliding at approximately 400–600 °C in an inert or low-oxidation atmosphere.
The effect may be diminished at lower sliding temperatures.
The effect may be diminished when oxidation is prominent.
The relative contributions of nanoprecipitates, Cu segregation, and twin density to any wear improvement are uncertain.
The untreated as-deposited coating serves as the experimental control.

Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in wear rate and microscopic deformation, or failure to observe the expected refined microstructure, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
